name: Bacterial infection pattern
interpretation: High WBC with neutrophilia, optionally immature granulocytes, suggests bacterial infection or inflammatory stress.

name: bacterial_infection_severe
interpretation: Marked leukocytosis (WBC 15.50) with dominant neutrophilia strongly suggests acute bacterial infection or severe systemic stress

name: anemia_chronic_disease
interpretation: Mild decrease in HGB in context of infection may indicate anemia of chronic disease or inflammation

name: severe_infection_thrombocytopenia
interpretation: Severe leukocytosis with thrombocytopenia – possible severe sepsis, DIC, or hematologic malignancy

name: mild_leukocytosis_neutrophilia
interpretation: WBC 10.2 (borderline) with NEUT_ABS 6.4 suggests mild neutrophilia – may represent early bacterial infection, physiologic stress (exercise, pain, corticosteroids), or resolving infectious process

name: borderline_monocytosis
interpretation: MONO% at 8.6% (upper borderline) in absence of significant leukocytosis may indicate a reactive state – chronic low-grade infection or early inflammatory process

name: Thrombocytopenia pattern
interpretation: Low platelet count suggests thrombocytopenia pattern and possible bleeding risk context.

name: thrombocytopenia
interpretation: Low platelet count – possible immune thrombocytopenia, bone marrow suppression, or viral infection

name: pancytopenia
interpretation: Pancytopenia – all cell lines low, consider aplastic anemia, bone marrow failure, or hypersplenism

name: monocytosis
interpretation: Elevated monocytes – consider chronic infection, autoimmune disease, or recovery from acute infection

name: bicytopenia_mild
interpretation: Concurrent mild anemia (HGB 139 g/L) and borderline thrombocytopenia (PLT 148) suggests bicytopenia – causes include hypersplenism, viral bone marrow suppression, or early myelodysplastic changes

name: reactive_monocytosis
interpretation: Absolute monocytosis (MONO_ABS 1.2, MONO% 9.4%) alongside neutrophilia suggests chronic or subacute infection, granulomatous inflammation, or tissue repair response

name: absolute_monocytosis
interpretation: Absolute monocytosis (MONO_ABS 0.9, MONO% 11.6%) without significant leukocytosis suggests chronic inflammatory stimulus – tuberculosis, chronic viral infection, inflammatory bowel disease, or early monocytic disorder

name: mild_anemia
interpretation: HGB 123 g/L represents mild anemia – in context of monocytosis, this may reflect anemia of chronic disease or underlying systemic condition driving both findings

name: Macrocytic anemia pattern
interpretation: Low hemoglobin with elevated MCV suggests a macrocytic anemia pattern.

name: megaloblastic_anemia
interpretation: Macrocytic anemia with high RDW – suggest B12 or folate deficiency (megaloblastic anemia)

name: normocytic_anemia_chronic_disease
interpretation: Low RBC (3.6), HGB (107 g/L), and HCT (31%) with normal morphology indices suggests normocytic anemia – anemia of chronic disease, renal anemia, or hemolytic process

name: reactive_monocytosis_neutrophilia
interpretation: Monocytosis (MONO% 7.4%) with neutrophilia suggests chronic infection, granulomatous disease, or inflammatory response; monocytes are key effectors in tissue repair and chronic inflammation

name: concurrent_anemia_inflammation
interpretation: Normocytic anemia combined with leukocyte shift (neutrophilia + monocytosis + relative lymphopenia) is consistent with anemia of inflammation or post-infection hematologic recovery

name: macrocytic_anemia
interpretation: HGB 90 g/L with MCV 97 fL (macrocytic) and markedly low RBC (2.8) points to megaloblastic anemia – vitamin B12 or folate deficiency are the most common causes; liver disease and hypothyroidism also considered

name: severe_anemia
interpretation: HGB at 90 g/L with HCT 27% and RBC 2.8 represents moderate-to-severe anemia requiring clinical evaluation for underlying etiology and assessment of transfusion need

name: monocytosis_chronic_disease
interpretation: Absolute monocytosis (MONO% 11%) in context of macrocytic anemia may indicate chronic inflammatory or nutritional deficiency with reactive monocyte response, or early myelodysplastic syndrome

name: bacterial_infection_neutrophilia
interpretation: WBC 12.8 with NEUT% 81.6% and absolute neutrophilia (10.5) combined with relative and absolute lymphopenia is a classic pattern of acute bacterial infection or significant physiologic stress

name: anemia_of_infection
interpretation: Mild anemia (HGB 115 g/L, RBC 3.9) in setting of active neutrophilia and monocytosis is consistent with anemia of inflammation – inflammatory cytokines inhibit erythropoiesis and iron utilization

name: lymphopenia_stress
interpretation: Absolute lymphopenia (LYM_ABS 0.8, LYM% 10.9%) alongside neutrophilia suggests stress-induced lymphocyte redistribution, steroid effect, or possible viral co-infection

name: eosinophilia_basophilia
interpretation: EOS% 10.6% and BASO% 1.6% above normal range – eosinophilia suggests parasitic infection, drug reaction, or allergic disease; concurrent basophilia may indicate myeloproliferative neoplasm or chronic inflammatory state

name: normocytic_anemia
interpretation: Low RBC (3.4), HGB (104 g/L), HCT (31%) with borderline-high MCV (93 fL) suggests normocytic to slightly macrocytic anemia – may be anemia of chronic disease or early megaloblastic change masked by concurrent process

name: reactive_monocytosis_lymphopenia
interpretation: Borderline monocytosis (MONO% 8.8%) with relative lymphopenia (LYM% 17.2%) suggests systemic inflammatory response – consistent with chronic parasitic infection, granulomatous disease, or tissue remodeling

name: lymphopenia
interpretation: Absolute lymphopenia (LYM_ABS 1.2) in absence of neutrophilia may reflect viral infection, immunosuppressive state, or steroid effect – warrants clinical correlation

name: microcytic_anemia
interpretation: HGB 115 g/L with low MCV (81 fL) and HCT (33%) is consistent with microcytic anemia – iron deficiency or thalassemia trait are the leading diagnoses

name: basophilia_monocytosis
interpretation: Mild basophilia (1.1%) with borderline monocytosis in context of microcytic anemia – basophilia may be reactive or signal early chronic myeloproliferative process; clinical follow-up recommended

name: eosinophilia
interpretation: Elevated eosinophils – consider allergic reaction, parasitic infection, or drug reaction

name: Microcytic anemia pattern
interpretation: Low hemoglobin with low MCV, often with high RDW, suggests a microcytic anemia pattern.

name: bacterial_infection
interpretation: WBC 19.47 with absolute neutrophilia (13.08 G/L) strongly suggests acute bacterial infection or significant physiologic stress

name: iron_deficiency_anemia
interpretation: Low HGB (125 g/L), MCV (77 fL), MCH (24 pg), and MCHC (319 g/L) are classic findings of microcytic hypochromic anemia – iron deficiency is the most common etiology

name: concurrent_anemia_infection
interpretation: Hypochromic anemia with active neutrophilia – iron deficiency may be compounded by anemia of acute inflammation; combined nutritional and inflammatory etiology is likely

name: thalassemia_trait
interpretation: Low MCV and MCH with normal RDW – microcytic anemia with uniform cell size, consistent with thalassemia trait

name: thrombocytosis
interpretation: High platelet count – consider reactive thrombocytosis (iron deficiency, infection) or essential thrombocythemia

name: microcytic_hypochromic_indices
interpretation: Low MCV (80 fL) and MCH (26 pg) indicate microcytic, hypochromic erythropoiesis without overt anemia – iron deficiency anemia or thalassemia trait are the primary differentials

name: iron_deficiency_reactive_thrombocytosis
interpretation: Microcytic (MCV 81 fL), hypochromic (MCH 26 pg) anemia with thrombocytosis (PLT 534) is a characteristic presentation of iron deficiency anemia – platelet elevation is a well-recognized reactive response to iron deficiency

name: severe_iron_deficiency_anemia
interpretation: Markedly low MCV (68 fL), MCH (21 pg), and MCHC (306 g/L) with HGB 105 g/L represents severe microcytic hypochromic anemia – iron deficiency is the most likely etiology at this degree of microcytosis

name: hypochromic_anemia
interpretation: Low MCH (21 pg) and MCHC (306 g/L) with HGB 105 g/L indicates hypochromic anemia – iron deficiency or thalassemia are primary differentials; serum ferritin and iron studies recommended

name: Viral infection pattern
interpretation: Lymphocytosis, sometimes with low WBC, may suggest viral infection pattern.

name: significant_basophilia
interpretation: BASO% 2.5% is markedly elevated – significant basophilia in the context of anemia and thrombocytosis should raise suspicion for chronic myeloid leukemia (CML) or other myeloproliferative neoplasm

name: concurrent_anemia_myeloproliferative
interpretation: The combination of microcytic anemia, reactive thrombocytosis, elevated basophils, and borderline lymphocytosis may represent a myeloproliferative process coexisting with iron deficiency

name: Renal impairment pattern
interpretation: High creatinine, often with high urea or potassium, suggests impaired renal function.

name: Tăng urê máu (Azotemia)
interpretation: Urê là sản phẩm thoái hóa protein, được thận lọc và bài tiết. Tăng urê phản ánh giảm chức năng lọc cầu thận hoặc tăng sản xuất từ dị hóa protein.

name: Tăng creatinine máu
interpretation: Creatinine là marker tin cậy hơn urê để đánh giá GFR. Tăng creatinine gợi ý giảm lọc cầu thận thực sự, ít bị ảnh hưởng bởi chế độ ăn hơn urê.

name: Tăng kali máu (Hyperkalemia)
interpretation: Hyperkalemia ảnh hưởng điện thế màng tế bào cơ tim, gây rối loạn nhịp nghiêm trọng. Cần loại trừ giả tăng (tan máu mẫu, tăng tiểu cầu) trước khi xử trí.

name: Hội chứng suy thận
interpretation: Tăng đồng thời UREA và CREATININE gợi ý giảm chức năng lọc cầu thận (azotemia). Cần phân biệt AKI (tăng cấp) vs CKD (tăng mạn).

name: Diabetes/glycemic abnormality pattern
interpretation: High glucose, especially with high HbA1c, suggests abnormal glycemic control.

name: Cardiac biomarker pattern
interpretation: Elevated cardiac biomarkers suggest myocardial injury or cardiac stress.

name: Tăng đường huyết
interpretation: Tăng glucose máu đói phản ánh suy giảm tiết insulin hoặc kháng insulin. Kết hợp HbA1c để đánh giá kiểm soát đường huyết dài hạn.

name: Tăng ALT
interpretation: ALT là enzyme đặc hiệu gan hơn AST. Tăng ALT chủ yếu gợi ý tổn thương tế bào gan (hepatocellular). ALT có thể tăng rất cao trong viêm gan cấp do virus.

name: Tăng CK-MB
interpretation: CK-MB là isoenzyme cơ tim của creatine kinase. Tăng trong AMI, nhưng ít đặc hiệu hơn Troponin T/I hiện đại.

name: HbA1c tăng
interpretation: HbA1c phản ánh mức đường huyết trung bình trong 2–3 tháng trước. Là tiêu chuẩn vàng theo dõi kiểm soát ĐTĐ dài hạn. Mỗi 1% HbA1c tương đương ~1.6 mmol/L glucose trung bình.

name: Tăng Troponin T
interpretation: Troponin T là biomarker tổn thương cơ tim đặc hiệu và nhạy nhất hiện nay. Bất kỳ tăng nào trên 99th percentile đều có ý nghĩa.

name: Hội chứng đái tháo đường kiểm soát kém
interpretation: Glucose cao và HbA1c tăng xác nhận đái tháo đường kiểm soát kém trong 2–3 tháng qua. Kết hợp rối loạn lipid và suy thận gợi ý biến chứng chuyển hóa.

name: Hội chứng vành cấp (ACS) / Tổn thương cơ tim
interpretation: Troponin T tăng gợi ý tổn thương tế bào cơ tim. Kết hợp với CK-MB tăng và bệnh cảnh lâm sàng đau ngực là nền tảng chẩn đoán ACS.

name: Tăng AST
interpretation: AST có trong nhiều mô: gan, cơ tim, cơ xương, thận. Tăng AST đơn độc có thể do nguồn ngoài gan; cần kết hợp với ALT và bối cảnh lâm sàng.

name: Iron store abnormality pattern
interpretation: High ferritin may reflect increased iron stores or inflammatory context.

name: Tăng acid uric máu (Hyperuricemia)
interpretation: Uric acid là sản phẩm thoái hóa purine. Tăng uric acid mạn tính gây lắng đọng monosodium urate crystals ở khớp (gout) và mô mềm (tophi), có thể gây sỏi thận urate.

name: Tăng ferritin máu
interpretation: Ferritin vừa là protein lưu trữ sắt vừa là reactant pha cấp (acute phase reactant). Tăng ferritin không đồng nghĩa với thừa sắt nếu có viêm đồng thời.

name: Tăng acid uric — Gout / Hội chứng chuyển hóa
interpretation: Tăng acid uric thường đi kèm hội chứng chuyển hóa. Kết hợp suy thận làm giảm bài tiết urate, tạo vòng luẩn quẩn.

name: Rối loạn dự trữ sắt
interpretation: Ferritin cao gợi ý quá tải sắt hoặc phản ứng viêm. Ferritin thấp là dấu hiệu thiếu sắt dự trữ đặc hiệu.

name: Dyslipidemia pattern
interpretation: Abnormal lipid profile suggests dyslipidemia and cardiovascular risk.

name: Tăng triglyceride máu (Hypertriglyceridemia)
interpretation: Triglyceride cao là yếu tố nguy cơ tim mạch và ở mức rất cao (>11.3 mmol/L) là nguy cơ viêm tụy cấp.

name: Giảm HDL-C (HDL thấp — yếu tố nguy cơ tim mạch ĐỘC LẬP)
interpretation: HDL-C thấp làm giảm khả năng vận chuyển cholesterol ngược về gan (reverse cholesterol transport), tăng nguy cơ xơ vữa động mạch.

name: Tăng LDL-C
interpretation: LDL-C là lipoprotein chính vận chuyển cholesterol đến mô, là yếu tố nguy cơ xơ vữa động mạch quan trọng nhất có thể điều chỉnh được.

name: Rối loạn lipid máu — Nguy cơ tim mạch cao
interpretation: Kết hợp tăng cholesterol/triglyceride với giảm HDL-C và/hoặc tăng LDL-C tạo thành bộ hồ sơ lipid atherogenic, nguy cơ xơ vữa động mạch cao.

name: left_shift_stress_response
interpretation: Elevated IG% (0.6%) indicates left shift – bone marrow stress or early infection releasing immature granulocytes into circulation

name: Hepatocellular injury pattern
interpretation: Elevation of ALT and AST suggests hepatocellular injury pattern.

name: Tăng cholesterol máu (Hypercholesterolemia)
interpretation: Cholesterol toàn phần bao gồm HDL-C, LDL-C và VLDL-C. Tăng cholesterol là yếu tố nguy cơ tim mạch chính, đặc biệt khi LDL-C tăng và HDL-C thấp.

name: Tổn thương tế bào gan (Hepatocellular injury)
interpretation: Tăng đồng thời AST và ALT gợi ý tổn thương hepatocellular. Tỉ lệ AST/ALT giúp định hướng nguyên nhân.

name: Hội chứng chuyển hóa
interpretation: Bộ xét nghiệm gợi ý hội chứng chuyển hóa: đề kháng insulin, rối loạn lipid máu atherogenic, và tăng acid uric. Nguy cơ tim mạch và ĐTĐ type 2 cao.

name: Polycythemia pattern
interpretation: High HGB/HCT, optionally elevated RBC, suggests polycythemia or erythrocytosis pattern.

name: polycythemia
interpretation: Elevated RBC, HGB, HCT – possible polycythemia vera or secondary polycythemia (hypoxia, dehydration)

name: polycythemia_erythrocytosis
interpretation: Elevated RBC (5.61), HGB (162 g/L), and HCT (49.6%) suggest absolute erythrocytosis – polycythemia vera or secondary causes (hypoxia, EPO-secreting tumor) should be considered

name: hyperchromic_macrocytic
interpretation: Elevated MCH and MCHC suggest hyperchromic red cells – consider macrocytic anemia (B12/folate deficiency) or hereditary spherocytosis

name: relative_neutropenia
interpretation: NEUT% below reference range – relative neutropenia, may reflect viral infection or lymphocyte predominance

name: neutropenia
interpretation: Severe neutropenia – risk of bacterial infection; consider drug-induced, autoimmune, or bone marrow failure
